verdict.reasoning: Doctor: "you've mentioned that you're not having much of an appetite and energy lately"; Patient: "have been feeling down" and agrees mood is low/depressed.

Patient: "like I'm feeling short of breath" and later "my heart starts beating and I can't really breath... in the lift"; Doctor labels these as palpitations: "you described them like palpitations to me".

Appetite: Patient: "three months ago, three and a half months ago" when joined new law firm. Weight: Doctor: "at least six months, would you say?" Patient: "Something like that"; amount: Patient: "less than a stone"; Doctor: "So about a stone".
Patient: "I feel nauseous every now and again" and when asked "Have you been ever sick with it?" replies "No, actually not."
Patient: "I don't really have problems when going to the toilet, it's just painless" and explicitly denies diarrhoea and blood/mucus: "no. No diarrhoea" and "no, no, nothing" to blood/mucus.
On respiratory: Patient: "no, not really" to cough. On chest pain: Doctor: "You get any chest pains with it?" Patient: "Not really, no"; Doctor: "OK, no chest pains."

Doctor: "you can walk about a mile and you don't feel short of breath at all." Patient: "That's right, yes." Later: "I haven't been walking lately at all... so like, it's really hard for me to identify when I feel the shortness of breath."
Patient: "I have trouble at work sometimes, having headaches, feeling nauseous."
Patient: "my, my, my wife was starting to complain as well, uh in, in nightly activities."
Patient: "I had too little activity of my thyroid"; Doctor clarifies: "underactive thyroid, yes." (hypothyroidism).
Patient: "In view of that, I took thyroxine" and later: "Uh, not anymore" and "I have not been taking it... since I changed doctor."
Patient: "who likes to be a lawyer?... Yes, of course I like" (occupation lawyer). Work and home: "work is OK" and "it is OK... other than that, it's OK" about home.

Low mood/fatigue/anorexia/weight loss/nausea: all described earlier ("feeling down", "not having much of an appetite", weight loss ~1 stone, intermittent nausea). Functioning: "I can do my work that's OK". No GI bleeding or vomiting: explicitly denies blood in stool and states "No, actually not" to being sick.

Palpitations and dyspnea in lift: Patient describes heart racing and inability to breathe in lift; Doctor: "you described them like palpitations to me". Exertional: Doctor confirms he can walk about a mile without SOB and no chest pain reported: "OK, no chest pains."

History: underactive thyroid confirmed. Off thyroxine since change of doctor: Patient: "not been taking it... since I changed doctor." Labs: Doctor: "When was your last blood test?" Patient: "haven't taken one in a long time" and Doctor: "So you've not had a blood test."
Doctor: "I think a general set of bloods is a good start... we look at things like anaemia, how your kidney functions are, your livers, all that, with vitamin levels."
Doctor: "I'll [do] the form for you, but in the interim you need to call support so that we can organise that blood test for you." and gives number in the app.
Doctor: "when you get the result, you will receive a text message through your phone to tell you to book an appointment."
Doctor: "If that's all clear, then we would need to do a physical examination" and reiterates "If labs are unremarkable, we then need to do" (implied in-person exam).
